title: GHA Indie Worker build server
description: The HTTP surface of `gha-indie-worker.rs` (src/http.rs `build_router`), transcribed from the code as it stands. Wire names are camelCase because every payload struct carries `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]`. Routes that answer with HTML, Prometheus text, a log stream, or a gzip artifact carry `client: false`: they belong in the map so the gate holds them to the source, but there is no typed JSON call to generate. NOTE: the server registers path parameters with Axum 0.7 `:job_id` syntax; this map uses the v2 `{job_id}` spelling, so the source comparison reports drift until the crate moves to Axum 0.8.

BuildJobId.doc: Server-minted build job id. A bare string on the wire, distinct here so a client cannot pass an arbitrary path segment.

BuildStatus.doc: `BuildStatus` in src/types.rs. Single-word camelCase variants are lowercase on the wire.

DeployRequest.doc: Optional controlled Kubernetes deploy attached to a build.

BuildRequest.doc: `BuildRequest` in src/types.rs. Only `repoUrl` is unconditionally required by the type; `image` and `profile` are required per `jobKind` by src/validation.rs, which the type system cannot express.

image.doc: `#[serde(default)]`: absent means the empty string, which validation rejects for image builds.

profile.doc: Operator-reviewed fixed command pipeline, for jobKind=run-profile.

requestId.doc: Caller-supplied idempotency id for at-least-once transports; duplicate ids are accepted and ignored.

BuildJobRecord.doc: `BuildJobRecord` in src/types.rs: the accepted job as the server echoes it back.

createdAtMs.doc: Milliseconds since the epoch. `u128` in Rust; no payload has ever exceeded i64.

lockKey.doc: fiducia.cloud lock key, when coordination is enabled.

ReadyResponse.doc: Answered with 200 when ready and 503 when not; the body is the same either way.

SyncOutcome.doc: `SyncOutcome` in src/gh_secrets.rs. Carries no secret value, only its fate.

SecretSyncRun.doc: One row of `gh_secret_sync_runs`. This entity has no `rename_all`, so its wire names are snake_case while the rest of this service is camelCase.

descriptor.summary: Self-describing service document: endpoints, job schema, profiles, and which optional subsystems are configured.
descriptor.doc: Built inline with `json!` from live configuration, so the shape is deliberately open.

healthz.summary: Liveness plus the effective allowlists and queue depth.

readyz.summary: Readiness: auth, work storage, and the required build tools.

api_docs_json.summary: The generated API document, served verbatim from generated/api-docs.json.

list_builds.doc: Deliberately untyped: with Postgres configured the handler appends persisted rows in a different shape from the live `BuildJobRecord` entries (see the report accompanying this map). Without Postgres every element is a BuildJobRecord.

submit_build.summary: Queue a build job. Answers 202 with the accepted record.
submit_build.doc: Queued through opto-sync because the server already treats submission as at-least-once: `requestId` is the caller-supplied idempotency key and duplicate ids are accepted and ignored.

get_build_logs.summary: The job's log file as text/plain.

get_build_artifacts.summary: The job's artifacts.tar.gz as an attachment stream.

github_webhook.doc: The handler takes the raw `Bytes` body so the HMAC in X-Hub-Signature-256 is verified over exactly what arrived; there is no typed request body to model, and the response shape varies by branch (ping, duplicate, accepted, rejected).

registry_webhook.summary: Container-registry image events, relayed onto NATS.
registry_webhook.doc: Raw `Bytes` body plus a shared-secret header and a required X-Delivery-Id; same reasoning as the GitHub webhook.

sync_secrets.summary: Run one GitHub Actions secret sync pass.
sync_secrets.doc: Takes no request body: the rules come from server configuration. The POST is the trigger.

sync_secrets_status.summary: The last 100 secret sync runs, newest first. Empty when Postgres is not configured.
